page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head and page number at the top. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: gratia, jura merito relaxantur, ut à thesi ad hypothesin mala fiat illatio.

7. Objicitur ab Acacio E-Georgius Acacius Enenck.nenckelo Barone, filius con-scius insidiarum in patrem, si non successerint, relegatur; quod si successerint, eadem poena, qua auctor criminis punitur.d. l. per l. 2. D. Ad l. Pompei de Parricid. Resp. Nulla hæc conse-quentia. Si injuste parens occidatur etiam cædis conscius filius punitur. Ergo si jure occidatur, itidem punietur filius? Absurda hæc illatio, & nullius momenti.

8. & ult. Objicitur. Decu-l. 4. l. ult. D. de Po-stulando [?].riones, qui contra patriam suas causas agere vetantur, pro parentibus tamen contra patriam agere possunt. Ut patriæ videantur parentes præponendi.
Resp. In causis civilibus & privatis non eadem ratio, quæ in publicis & criminalibus.

page.notes: The first note block reads "Georgius Acacius Enenck." and the second "d. l. per l. 2. D. Ad l. Pompei de Parricid." The note beside paragraph 8 reads "l. 4. l. ult. D. de Postulando"; the word "Postulando" is uncertain because the first letters are worn, so it is marked [?]. The side placement of the notes is taken from the scan. The catchword "Præ-" is at the foot right. The page number 113 is printed at the top right, and the running head "De Duellis." at the top centre.
